chapter_seo_title: The Beheader: Li Huowang Hunts the Mercenary King in a Supernatural Ambush
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang ambushes the Mercenary King mid-performance, only to face a skin-man escape, shadow-puppet immobilization, and two corrupted Wealth Gods. A desperate sprint toward the Great Qi fissure.
og_title: Li Huowang Hunts the Mercenary King—With a Reality-Splitting Sword
og_description: Li Huowang’s ambush goes sideways. The Mercenary King has a skin-man backup, two Wealth God bodyguards, and an army of shadow puppets. Can our one-armed hero reach the Great Qi tear in time?
twitter_title: The Beheader: Li Huowang’s Reality-Splitting Sword vs. The Wealth Gods
twitter_description: Li Huowang loses a hand, gains a dimensional escape plan, and learns that the Mercenary King doesn’t stay dead easily.

lore_anchors.definition: A life-preserving artifact in Dao-Twisted cultivation; a palm-sized doll made from the user’s own skin or hair that can regrow a destroyed body if the original consciousness transfers into it.
A folk deity of worldly prosperity, often depicted with a gold ingot; in this chapter, a masked bodyguard wearing this title controls any copper-coin weaponry through sympathetic magic.
A warrior-aspect of the Wealth God, often mounted and armored; in this story, he manifests as a silver-mace-wielding, leopard-riding enforcer.
Supernatural beings that mimic the art of Chinese shadow puppetry; they can seize a living person’s shadow to immobilize them, and are nullified by the absence of light.
A ritual Daoist weapon composed of old Chinese coins strung on red cord; in the Dao-Twisted World, it is vulnerable to the control of Wealth God imitators.
A cut in reality that tears open a portal to the Great Qi realm; Li Huowang can use it both as a weapon and as a dimensional stepping-stone.
